`2021 – 2024`

**Topics:** onshore wind · lender E&S requirements · biodiversity · resettlement · Indigenous Peoples

**My contributions:** environmental fieldwork, baseline study, impact assessment, noise · shadow flicker · visual modelling

**Skills used:** WindPro, R, QGIS, AIIB Environmental and Social Framework

**Official project page:** [AIIB – Viet Nam: Dak Lak Wind Power Project (No. 000509)](https://www.aiib.org/en/projects/details/2023/proposed/Viet-Nam-Dak-Lak-Wind-Power-Project.html)

## Project at a glance

| | |
|---|---|
| **Capacity** | 200 MW, four 50 MW wind farms |
| **Phase 1** | Krong Buk 1, Krong Buk 2, Cu Ne 1 |
| **Phase 2** | Cu Ne 2 |
| **Location** | Dak Lak Province, Central Highlands, Vietnam |
| **Sponsor** | China Huadian Engineering Company Limited |
| **Lender** | Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) |
| **Financing** | USD 100 million, non-sovereign long-term debt |
| **Offtake** | Long-term power purchase agreements with EVN |
| **E&S category** | Category A (highest risk level) |

## Overview

The project develops four 50 MW wind farms in Dak Lak Province, built in two phases, and sells power to Vietnam Electricity (EVN) under long-term power purchase agreements. AIIB proposed USD 100 million in long-term financing for construction.

## Key environmental & social issues

As a **Category A** project, it carries significant potential impacts:

- **Biodiversity:** collision risk for birds and bats, with eight Key Biodiversity Areas and six Protected Areas within 50 km
- **Community health & safety:** noise, shadow flicker and blade throw
- **Land & livelihoods:** physical and economic displacement, including Ethnic Minority households in Krong Buk District

## Closing the gap to lender standards

The original ESIA was prepared under Vietnamese law and did not fully meet AIIB requirements. To close the gap, a **Corrective Environmental and Social Action Plan (CESAP)** set out ten areas of work, including:

- an updated Stakeholder Engagement Plan
- a Land Acquisition Audit
- a Resettlement, Livelihood Restoration and Community Development Plan
- a Biodiversity Management Plan and a Birds Adaptive Management Plan
- project-level grievance mechanisms for communities and workers, with third-party review

## My role

- Supervised environmental fieldwork covering water, soil, air and noise
- Authored the **Environmental Baseline** chapter, describing the site's climatic, hydrological and topographical conditions
- Authored ESIA/ESMP impact chapters on **surface water, groundwater, air, noise and soil**
- Modelled and assessed **noise, shadow flicker and visual impacts** of the wind turbines using **WindPro, R and QGIS**
